positive_text: Determine the number of $8 \times 8$ matrices with entries in $\{1, 2\}$ such that the sum of each row and each column is odd.

negatives.text: Find the number of ways one can put numbers $1$ or $2$ in each cell of a $8 \times 8$ chessboard in such a way that the sum of numbers in each column and in each row is an even number.

Find the number of ways one can put numbers $1$ or $2$ in each cell of a $8 \times 8$ chessboard in such a way that the sum of numbers in each row is odd and the sum of numbers in each column is even.
Find the number of ways one can put numbers $1$ or $2$ in each cell of a $8 \times 8$ chessboard in such a way that the sum of numbers in each row and in each column is a multiple of $3$.

positive_text:
Suppose a convex polygon is triangulated into triangles, and let $V$ be the set of all vertices and $E$ the set of all edges from the triangulation. A polygon is called good if:

1. No three points in $V$ are collinear;

2. Every vertex in $V$ is incident to an even number of edges in $E$.

Determine all such good polygons.

negatives.text:
A convex polygon is divided into triangles with vertex set $V$ and edge set $E$. The polygon is said to be good if:

i. No three vertices in $V$ are collinear;

ii. Each vertex in $V$ belongs to an odd number of edges in $E$.

Find all good polygons.

A convex polygon is divided into triangles with vertex set $V$ and edge set $E$. The polygon is said to be good if:

i. No three vertices in $V$ are collinear;

ii. Each vertex in $V$ belongs to an even number of edges in $E$, excluding the boundary edges.

Find all good polygons.

A convex polygon is divided into triangles with vertex set $V$ and edge set $E$. The polygon is said to be good if:

i. No three vertices in $V$ are collinear;

ii. Each vertex in $V$ belongs to an even number of edges in $E$, except for one vertex.

Find all good polygons.

positive_text: On a standard $8\times 8$ chessboard, where cells alternate between black and white, define a diagonal trail as a sequence of unique white squares such that each pair of consecutive squares shares exactly one corner or edge. What is the minimum number of such diagonal trails required to cover all white squares?

negatives.text: A chessboard has $64$ cells painted black and white in the usual way. A bishop path is a sequence of distinct cells such that two consecutive cells share an edge. At least how many bishop paths can the set of all white cells be divided into?

A chessboard has $64$ cells painted black and white in the usual way. A bishop path is a sequence of distinct cells such that two consecutive cells share a diagonal and are of the same color. At least how many bishop paths can the set of all white cells be divided into?

A chessboard has $64$ cells painted black and white in the usual way. A bishop path is a sequence of distinct cells such that two consecutive cells share exactly one common point. At least how many bishop paths can the set of all black and white cells be divided into?

positive_text:
Let $ABC$ be a triangle with $M, N, P$ as the midpoints of $BC, CA, AB$, respectively. Let $I$ be the intersection point of the internal angle bisectors of $\angle PBM$ and $\angle NMP$, and $J$ be the intersection point of the internal angle bisectors of $\angle NCM$ and $\angle PMN$. Let $\omega_{1}$ be the circle centered at $I$ and tangent to $MP$ at $D$, and $\omega_{2}$ be the circle centered at $J$ and tangent to $MN$ at $E$.

1. Show that $DE$ is parallel to $BC$.

2. Show that the radical axis of $\omega_{1}$ and $\omega_{2}$ bisects $DE$.

negatives.text:
Let $ABC$ be a triangle with $M, N, P$ as the midpoints of $BC, CA, AB$, respectively. Suppose that $I$ is the intersection of angle bisectors of $\angle BPM$, $\angle MNP$ and $J$ is the intersection of angle bisectors of $\angle CNM$, $\angle MPN$. Denote ($\omega_{1}$) as the circle of center $I$ and tangent to $MP$ at $D$, $\left(\omega_{2}\right)$ as the circle of center $J$ and tangent to $MN$ at $E$.

1. Prove that $DE$ is perpendicular to $BC$.

2. Prove that the radical axis of two circles ($\omega_{1}$), ($\omega_{2}$) bisects the segment $DE$.

Let $ABC$ be a triangle with $M, N, P$ as the midpoints of $BC, CA, AB$, respectively. Suppose that $I$ is the intersection of angle bisectors of $\angle BPM$, $\angle MNP$ and $J$ is the intersection of angle bisectors of $\angle CNM$, $\angle MPN$. Denote ($\omega_{1}$) as the circle of center $I$ and tangent to $MP$ at $D$, $\left(\omega_{2}\right)$ as the circle of center $J$ and tangent to $MN$ at $E$.

1. Prove that $DE$ is parallel to $AC$.

2. Prove that the radical axis of two circles ($\omega_{1}$), ($\omega_{2}$) bisects the segment $DE$.

Let $ABC$ be a triangle with $M, N, P$ as the midpoints of $BC, CA, AB$, respectively. Suppose that $I$ is the intersection of angle bisectors of $\angle BPM$, $\angle MNP$ and $J$ is the intersection of angle bisectors of $\angle CNM$, $\angle MPN$. Denote ($\omega_{1}$) as the circle of center $I$ and tangent to $MP$ at $D$, $\left(\omega_{2}\right)$ as the circle of center $J$ and tangent to $MN$ at $E$.

1. Prove that $DE$ is parallel to $BC$.

2. Prove that the radical axis of two circles ($\omega_{1}$), ($\omega_{2}$) trisects the segment $DE$.

positive_text: Determine all positive integers $n$ for which $n^{2} + 3$ is divisible by Euler's totient function $\varphi(n)$.

negatives.text: Find all positive integers $n$ such that $\varphi(n)$ is a divisor of $n^{2} - 3$.
Find all positive integers $n$ such that $\varphi(n)$ is a divisor of $n^{2} + 3n$.
Find all positive integers $n$ such that $\varphi(n^{2})$ is a divisor of $n^{2} + 3$.

positive_text:
Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle with circumcenter $O$ and orthocenter $H$. Let $M$ lie on the minor arc $BC$ of the circumcircle of triangle $ABC$, not at $B$ or $C$. Let $D, E, F$ be the reflections of $M$ across $OA, OB, OC$ respectively. Let $BF$ and $CE$ intersect at $K$, and let $I$ be the incenter of triangle $DEF$.

1. Prove that the perpendicular bisectors of segments $EF$ and $IK$ intersect on the circumcircle of triangle $ABC$.

2. Prove that points $H$, $K$, and $I$ are collinear.

negatives.text:
Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle with circumcenter $O$ and orthocenter $H$. Let $M$ lie on the arc $BC$ of the circumcircle of triangle $ABC$ not containing $A$. Let $D, E, F$ be the reflections of $M$ across $OA, OB, OC$. Let $BF$ and $CE$ intersect at $K$, and let $I$ be the circumcenter of triangle $DEF$.

1. Prove that the perpendicular bisectors of $EF$ and $IK$ meet on the circumcircle of triangle $ABC$.

2. Prove that $H, K, I$ are collinear.

Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle with circumcenter $O$ and orthocenter $H$. Let $M$ lie on the arc $BC$ of the circumcircle of triangle $ABC$ not containing $A$. Let $D, E, F$ be the reflections of $M$ across $OA, OB, OC$. Let $BF$ and $CE$ intersect at $K$, and let $I$ be the incenter of triangle $DEF$.

1. Prove that the perpendicular bisectors of $EF$ and $IK$ meet at a point outside the circumcircle of triangle $ABC$.

2. Prove that $H, K, I$ are collinear.

Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle with circumcenter $O$ and orthocenter $H$. Let $M$ lie on the arc $BC$ of the circumcircle of triangle $ABC$ not containing $A$. Let $D, E, F$ be the reflections of $M$ across $OA, OB, OC$. Let $BF$ and $CE$ intersect at $K$, and let $I$ be the incenter of triangle $DEF$.

1. Prove that the perpendicular bisectors of $EF$ and $IK$ meet at a point on the circumcircle of triangle $DEF$.

2. Prove that $H, K, I$ are collinear.

positive_text: Find the largest number of non-overlapping 5-cell cross shapes (with arms of length 2 in all directions) that can fit in an $8 \times 8$ grid where the cross axes are aligned with the grid edges.

negatives.text: Determine the maximal number of disjoint crosses (5 squares) which can be put inside a $9 \times 9$ chessboard such that sides of a cross are parallel to sides of the chessboard.
Determine the maximal number of disjoint crosses (5 squares) which can be put inside $8 \times 8$ chessboard such that the cross is rotated at 45 degrees relative to the sides of the chessboard.

Determine the maximal number of disjoint crosses (5 squares) which can be put inside an $8 \times 8$ chessboard such that sides of a cross are parallel to sides of the chessboard and each cross is placed on a different color square.

positive_text: Let $I$ be the incenter of triangle $ABC$, and let $J$ be the excenter opposite to vertex $A$. If $M$ is the midpoint of segment $BC$ and $N$ is the midpoint of the arc $BAC$ of the circumcircle of triangle $ABC$, and $T$ is the reflection of $N$ over point $A$, show that $J, M, I, T$ lie on a circle.

negatives.text: Let $I$ be the incenter of triangle $ABC$ and $J$ the excenter of the side $BC$. Let $M$ be the midpoint of $CB$ and $N$ the midpoint of arc $BAC$ of circle $(ABC)$. If $T$ is the symmetric of the point $N$ by the point $B$, prove that the quadrilateral $JMI T$ is cyclic.

Let $I$ be the incenter of triangle $ABC$ and $J$ the excenter of the side $BC$. Let $M$ be the midpoint of $CB$ and $N$ the midpoint of arc $BAC$ of circle $(ABC)$. If $T$ is the symmetric of the point $N$ by the point $A$, prove that the quadrilateral $JMI T$ is tangential.

positive_text: Suppose the set $\mathbb{Z}$ is colored using three distinct colors. Show that there exist two integers of the same color such that their difference is a perfect square.

negatives.text: Each integer is painted one of three colors. Prove that there exist two distinct numbers of the same color, whose sum is a perfect square.
Each integer is painted one of three colors. Prove that there exist two distinct numbers of the same color, whose product is a perfect square.
Each integer is painted one of three colors. Prove that there exist two distinct numbers of the same color, whose difference is a cube.

positive_text: Determine the maximum total number of black and white queens that can be placed on an $8 \times 8$ board without any queen attacking another, regardless of color.

negatives.text: What is the biggest number of black and white queens one can place on a chessboard, such that no queen of the same color attacks another?
What is the biggest number of black and white queens one can place on a chessboard, such that no two of the same color beat one another?

positive_text: Let $E$ be a point inside the parallelogram $ABCD$ such that $\angle BAE = \angle BCE$. Prove that the circumcenters of triangles $DAE$, $CDE$, $BCE$, and $ABE$ lie on a common circle.

negatives.text: Let $E$ be a point inside the parallelogram $ABCD$ such that $\angle BAE = \angle ECD$. Prove that the circumcenters of triangles $ABE$, $BCE$, $CDE$, $DAE$ are concyclic.
Let $E$ be a point inside the parallelogram $ABCD$ such that $\angle BAE = \angle BDE$. Prove that the circumcenters of triangles $ABE$, $BCE$, $CDE$, $DAE$ are concyclic.

positive_text: Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle with distinct side lengths, where $O$ and $H$ denote the circumcenter and orthocenter, respectively. Show that the nine-point circles of triangles $AHO$, $BHO$, and $CHO$ intersect at exactly two points.

negatives.text: Let $ABC$ be an acute, non-isosceles triangle with $O$, $H$ as circumcenter and orthocenter, respectively. Prove that the nine-point circles of $ABO$, $BCO$, and $CAO$ have two common points.
Let $ABC$ be an acute, non-isosceles triangle with $O$, $H$ as circumcenter and orthocenter, respectively. Prove that the nine-point circles of $AHO$, $BHO$, $CHO$ have three common points.
Let $ABC$ be an acute, non-isosceles triangle with $O$, $H$ as circumcenter and orthocenter, respectively. Prove that the nine-point circles of $AHO$, $BHO$, $CHO$ are tangent to each other.

positive_text: In triangle $ABC$, let the circle with diameter $BC$ intersect $AB$ and $AC$ at $F$ and $E$, respectively. Let $P$ be a point on this circle. If $B_{0}$ and $C_{0}$ are the feet of perpendiculars from $P$ to $AC$ and $AB$, respectively, and $H$ is the orthocenter of triangle $AB_{0}C_{0}$, prove that $\angle EHF = 90^\circ$.

negatives.text: Let $ABC$ be a triangle, the circle having $BC$ as diameter cuts $AB$, $AC$ at $F$, $E$ respectively. Let $P$ be a point on this circle. Let $C_{0}$, $B_{0}$ be the projections of $P$ upon the sides $AB$, $AC$ respectively. Let $H$ be the orthocenter of triangle $AB_{0}C_{0}$. Show that $\angle EHP = 90^\circ$.

Let $ABC$ be a triangle, the circle having $BC$ as diameter cuts $AB$, $AC$ at $F$, $E$ respectively. Let $P$ be a point on this circle. Let $C_{0}$, $B_{0}$ be the projections of $P$ upon the sides $AB$, $AC$ respectively. Let $H$ be the centroid of triangle $AB_{0}C_{0}$. Show that $\angle EHF = 90^\circ$.

Let $ABC$ be a triangle, the circle having $BC$ as diameter cuts $AB$, $AC$ at $F$, $E$ respectively. Let $P$ be a point on this circle. Let $C_{0}$, $B_{0}$ be the projections of $P$ upon the sides $AB$, $AC$ respectively. Let $H$ be the orthocenter of triangle $AB_{0}C_{0}$. Show that $\angle EHF = 45^\circ$.

positive_text: Given that among $a + b$, $a - b$, $ab$, and $\frac{a}{b}$, there are exactly two positive and two negative expressions, determine the sign of $b$.

negatives.text: Among numbers $a + b$, $a - b$, $ab$, $\frac{a}{b}$ exactly three are positive and one is negative. Find the sign of $b$.
Among numbers $a + b$, $a - b$, $ab$, $\frac{a}{b}$ exactly two are positive and exactly two are negative. Find the sign of $a$.
Among numbers $a + b$, $a - b$, $ab$, $\frac{a}{b}$ exactly two are positive and exactly two are negative. Find the sign of $a + b$.

positive_text: Let $ABC$ be a triangle with fixed side $BC$ and vertex $A$ moving on a fixed circle $(O)$. Let $H$ be the orthocenter of triangle $ABC$, and suppose points $D$ and $E$ lie on $AB$ and $AC$, respectively, such that $H$ is the midpoint of segment $DE$. Prove that the center of the circumcircle of triangle $ADE$ lies on a fixed circle as $A$ moves along $(O)$.

negatives.text: Let triangle $ABC$ be inscribed in a fixed circle $(O)$ with $BC$ fixed and $A$ varying on $(O)$. Let $H$ be the orthocenter of triangle $ABC$, and take $D$, $E$ on $AB$, $AC$ respectively such that $H$ lies on segment $DE$ but is not its midpoint. Prove that when $A$ moves on $(O)$, the center of $(ADE)$ belongs to a fixed circle.

Let triangle $ABC$ be inscribed in a fixed circle $(O)$ with $BC$ fixed and $A$ varying on $(O)$. Let $H$ be the orthocenter of triangle $ABC$, and take $D$, $E$ on $AB$, $AC$ respectively such that $H$ is the midpoint of $DE$. Prove that when $A$ moves on $(O)$, the center of $(ADE)$ lies on a fixed line.

Let triangle $ABC$ be inscribed in a fixed circle $(O)$ with $BC$ fixed and $A$ varying on $(O)$. Let $H$ be the orthocenter of triangle $ABC$, and take $D$, $E$ on $AB$, $AC$ respectively such that $H$ is the midpoint of $DE$. Prove that when $A$ moves on $(O)$, the center of $(ADE)$ lies on a fixed circle centered at $H$.

positive_text: Let $ABC$ be an acute, non-isosceles triangle with incenter $I$ and circumcenter $O$. The incircle $(I)$ touches $BC$, $CA$, and $AB$ at $D$, $E$, and $F$ respectively. Let $EF$ intersect the circumcircle $(O)$ of triangle $ABC$ at points $P$ and $Q$. Prove that the circle passing through $P$, $Q$, and $D$ bisects segment $BC$.

negatives.text: Let $ABC$ be an acute, non-isosceles triangle with circumcenter $O$, incenter $I$, and incircle $(I)$ tangent to $BC$, $CA$, $AB$ at $D$, $E$, $F$ respectively. Suppose that $EF$ cuts $(O)$ at $P$, $Q$. Prove that $(PQD)$ bisects segment $AC$.

Let $ABC$ be an acute, non-isosceles triangle with circumcenter $O$, incenter $I$, and incircle $(I)$ tangent to $BC$, $CA$, $AB$ at $D$, $E$, $F$ respectively. Suppose that $DE$ cuts $(O)$ at $P$, $Q$. Prove that $(PQD)$ bisects segment $BC$.

Let $ABC$ be an acute, non-isosceles triangle with circumcenter $O$, incenter $I$, and incircle $(I)$ tangent to $BC$, $CA$, $AB$ at $D$, $E$, $F$ respectively. Suppose that $EF$ cuts $(O)$ at $P$, $Q$. Prove that $(PQD)$ bisects segment $BC$ in the direction of $B$.

positive_text: Let $A, B, C, D, E, F$ be points on a circle $O$ in counterclockwise order. If $CF$ is perpendicular to $BD$ and the lines $CF, BE, AD$ meet at a common point, let $M$ be the foot of the perpendicular from $B$ to $AC$, and $N$ be the foot of the perpendicular from $D$ to $CE$. Prove that $AE$ is parallel to $MN$.

negatives.text: On circle $O$, points $A, B, C, D, E, F$ are arranged in counterclockwise order. Given that $CF$ is perpendicular to $BD$, and the lines $CF, BE, AD$ are concurrent, define $M$ as the foot of the perpendicular from $B$ to $AB$, and $N$ as the foot of the perpendicular from $D$ to $DE$. Prove that $AE$ is parallel to $MN$.

Let six points $A, B, C, D, E, F$ lie on a circle $O$ in counterclockwise order. Suppose $CF$ is perpendicular to $BD$, and the lines $CF, BE, AD$ are concurrent. If $M$ is the midpoint of $AC$, and $N$ is the midpoint of $CE$, prove that $AE$ is parallel to $MN$.

positive_text: Do there exist pairwise distinct positive integers $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_{101}, y_1, y_2, \ldots, y_{101}$ such that for every non-empty subset $T$ of $\{1, 2, \ldots, 101\}$, the value $\sum_{i \in T} x_i$ divides $100! + \sum_{i \in T} y_i$?

Define a set of positive integers as nice if the number of elements in the set is equal to the mean of the elements. A positive integer $n$ is called amazing if the set $\{1, 2, \ldots, n\}$ can be divided into nice subsets.

a) Prove that all squares of positive integers are amazing.

b) Demonstrate that there are infinitely many integers that are not amazing.

negatives.text:
Let us call a set of positive integers nice if the number of its elements is greater than the average of its numbers. Call a positive integer $n$ an amazing number if the set $\{1, 2, \ldots, n\}$ can be partitioned into nice subsets.

a) Prove that every perfect square is amazing

b) Show that there are infinitely many positive integers which are not amazing.

Let us call a set of positive integers nice if the number of its elements equals to the product of its numbers. Call a positive integer $n$ an amazing number if the set $\{1, 2, \ldots, n\}$ can be partitioned into nice subsets.

a) Prove that every perfect square is amazing

b) Show that there are infinitely many positive integers which are not amazing.

Let us call a set of positive integers nice if the number of its elements is equal to the average of its numbers. Call a positive integer $n$ an amazing number if the set $\{1, 2, \ldots, n\}$ can be partitioned into nice subsets with the sum of their elements being a perfect square.

a) Prove that every perfect square is amazing

b) Show that there are infinitely many positive integers which are not amazing.

positive_text: What is the maximum number of $3 \times 2 \times 3$ bricks that can be fit inside a $9 \times 8 \times 8$ box?

negatives.text: What is the maximum number of $2 \times 3 \times 3$ bricks that can be fit inside an $8 \times 8 \times 8$ box?
What is the maximum number of $3 \times 3 \times 3$ bricks that can be fit inside an $8 \times 8 \times 9$ box?

positive_text: Let $BB'$, $CC'$ be the altitudes of an acute-angled triangle $ABC$. Two circles passing through $A$ and $C'$ are tangent to $BC$ at points $P$ and $Q$. Prove that the points $A$, $B'$, $P$, and $Q$ lie on a single circle.

negatives.text: Let $BB'$, $CC'$ be the altitudes of an acute-angled triangle $ABC$. Two circles passing through $A$ and $C'$ are tangent to $AB$ at points $P$ and $Q$. Prove that $A$, $B'$, $P$, $Q$ are concyclic.

Let $BB'$, $CC'$ be the altitudes of an acute-angled triangle $ABC$. Two circles passing through $A$ and $C'$ are tangent to the line $BC$ at points $P$ and $Q$. Prove that $A$, $B'$, $P$, $Q$ are collinear.

positive_text:
Show that if $m$ and $n$ are positive integers such that $m \geq 1$, $n \geq 1$, and $(m, n) \neq (1, 1)$, then the sum
$$
\sum_{k = 0}^{n - 1} \frac{1}{m + k}
$$
cannot be an integer.

negatives.text:
Prove that for any 2 positive integers $m$ and $n$ with $(m, n) \neq (1, 1)$ the value of expression
$$
\frac{1}{m} + \frac{1}{m+1} + \dots + \frac{1}{m+n-1}
$$
is an integer.

Prove that for any 2 positive integers $m$ and $n$ with $(m, n) \neq (1, 1)$ the value of expression
$$
\frac{1}{m^2} + \frac{1}{(m+1)^2} + \dots + \frac{1}{(m+n-1)^2}
$$
is not an integer.

Prove that for any 2 positive integers $m$ and $n$ with $(m, n) \neq (1, 1)$ the value of expression
$$
\frac{1}{m} + \frac{1}{m+1} + \dots + \frac{1}{m+n-1}
$$
is not a rational number.

positive_text:
Determine how many integers $ x $ satisfy the identity
$$
\left\lfloor \frac{x}{7} \right\rfloor - \left\lfloor \frac{x}{17} \right\rfloor = \left\lfloor \frac{x}{12} \right\rfloor.
$$

negatives.text:
Find the number of integer solutions of the equation
$$
\left\lfloor \frac{x}{7} \right\rfloor = \left\lfloor \frac{x}{12} \right\rfloor + \left\lfloor \frac{x}{17} \right\rfloor + 1.
$$

Find the number of integer solutions of the equation
$$
\left\lfloor \frac{x}{7} \right\rfloor = \left\lfloor \frac{x}{12} \right\rfloor - \left\lfloor \frac{x}{17} \right\rfloor.
$$

Find the number of integer solutions of the inequality
$$
\left\lfloor \frac{x}{7} \right\rfloor > \left\lfloor \frac{x}{12} \right\rfloor + \left\lfloor \frac{x}{17} \right\rfloor.
$$

positive_text:
Let $f: \mathbb{R}^{+} \to \mathbb{R}^{+}$ be such that
$$
f(a + 2b + f(a + b)) = f(2a) + f(3b), \forall a, b > 0.
$$
1. Determine all functions $f(a)$ satisfying the condition.
2. Suppose that $f(4\sin^4a)f(4\cos^4a) \ge f^2(1)$ for all $a \in (0; \frac{\pi}{2})$. Find the minimum value of $f(2022)$.

negatives.text:
Let $f: \mathbb{R}^{+} \to \mathbb{R}^{+}$ satisfy
$$
f(x + 2y + f(x + y)) = f(2x) + f(3y), \forall x, y > 0.
$$
1. Find all functions $f(x)$ that satisfy the condition.
2. Suppose that $f(4\sin^4x)f(4\cos^4x) < f^2(1)$ for all $x \in (0; \frac{\pi}{2})$. Find the minimum value of $f(2022)$.

Let $f: \mathbb{R}^{+} \to \mathbb{R}^{+}$ satisfy
$$
f(x + 2y + f(x + y)) = f(2x) + f(3y), \forall x, y > 0.
$$
1. Find all functions $f(x)$ that satisfy the condition.
2. Suppose that $f(4\sin^4x)f(4\cos^4x) = f^2(1)$ for all $x \in (0; \frac{\pi}{2})$. Find the minimum value of $f(2022)$.

Let $f: \mathbb{R}^{+} \to \mathbb{R}^{+}$ satisfy
$$
f(x + 2y + f(x + y)) = f(2x) + f(3y), \forall x, y > 0.
$$
1. Find all functions $f(x)$ that satisfy the condition.
2. Suppose that $f(4\sin^2x)f(4\cos^2x) \ge f^2(1)$ for all $x \in (0; \frac{\pi}{2})$. Find the minimum value of $f(2022)$.

positive_text:
Let $S = \{1, 2, ..., n\}$, where each element is assigned a color (red or blue), with both colors appearing at least once. It is known that
* Each red element is the sum of two distinct blue elements;
* Each blue element is the difference of two red elements.
Determine the smallest possible value of $n$ for which this coloring is feasible.

negatives.text:
Each integer from $1$ to $n$ was colored either red or blue, with both colors used. It turned out that
* Every red number is a sum of some two distinct blue numbers;
* Every blue number is the sum of some two red numbers.
Find the smallest $n$ for which such coloring is possible.

Each integer from $1$ to $n$ was colored either red or blue, with both colors used. It turned out that
* Every red number is a product of two distinct blue numbers;
* Every blue number is a difference of two red numbers.
Find the smallest $n$ for which such coloring is possible.

Each integer from $1$ to $n$ was colored either red or blue, with both colors used. It turned out that
* Every red number is a sum of some two distinct blue numbers;
* Every blue number is a sum of some two red numbers.
Find the smallest $n$ for which such coloring is possible.

positive_text: Let $\mathbb{N}$ be the set of positive integers. Determine all functions $f: \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ such that $a - b$ divides $a^{f(a)} - b^{f(b)}$ for all coprime $a, b \in \mathbb{N}$.

negatives.text: Let $\mathbb{N}$ be the set of positive integers. Find all functions $f: \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ such that $x - y$ divides $x^{f(y)} - y^{f(x)}$ for every two coprime integers $x$ and $y$.
Let $\mathbb{N}$ be the set of positive integers. Find all functions $f: \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ such that $x + y$ divides $x^{f(x)} - y^{f(y)}$ for every two coprime integers $x$ and $y$.
Let $\mathbb{N}$ be the set of positive integers. Find all functions $f: \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ such that $x - y$ divides $x^{f(x)} + y^{f(y)}$ for every two coprime integers $x$ and $y$.

positive_text: Let triangle $ABC$ be an acute scalene triangle inscribed in a circle $k$, and let $D$ be the point on side $BC$ where the angle bisector of $\angle ABC$ intersects it. For any point $I$ on segment $AD$, define $H$ as the foot of the perpendicular from $I$ to $BC$. Let $\omega$ be a circle centered at $I$ with radius $IH$, and let $U$ be the internal homothety center of circles $k$ and $\omega$. Prove that $U$ lies on a fixed line as $I$ moves along $AD$, and that $AI$ is the angle bisector of $\angle HAU$.

negatives.text: Let triangle $ABC$ be an acute scalene triangle inscribed in a circle $k$. The bisector of angle $\angle ABC$ meets side $BC$ at point $D$. Let $I$ be an arbitrary point on the segment $AD$, and let $H$ be the projection of $I$ onto line $BC$. Circle $\omega$ is centered at $I$ and passes through $H$, and $U$ is the external homothety center of the circles $k$ and $\omega$. Prove that $U$ lies on a fixed line as $I$ moves on $AD$, and that $AI$ bisects the angle $\angle HAU$.

An acute scalene triangle $ABC$ is inscribed in a circle $k$. The bisector of angle $\angle ABC$ meets side $BC$ at point $D$. Let $I$ be an arbitrary point on the segment $AD$, and let $H$ be the projection of $I$ onto line $BC$. Circle $\omega$ is centered at $I$ and passes through $H$, and $U$ is the internal homothety center of the circles $k$ and $\omega$. Prove that $U$ lies on a fixed line as $I$ moves on $AD$, and that $AI$ trisects the angle $\angle HAU$.

An acute scalene triangle $ABC$ is inscribed in a circle $k$. The bisector of angle $\angle ABC$ meets side $BC$ at point $D$. Let $I$ be an arbitrary point on the segment $AD$, and let $H$ be the projection of $I$ onto line $BC$. Circle $\omega$ is centered at $I$ and passes through $H$, and $U$ is the internal homothety center of the circles $k$ and $\omega$. Prove that $U$ lies on a fixed circle as $I$ moves on $AD$, and that $AI$ bisects the angle $\angle HAU$.

positive_text:
Let $b_1, b_2, \dots, b_n$ be integers such that $\sum_{i=1}^{n} b_i = 2022$, and let $a$ be a divisor of $\left\lfloor \dfrac{2022!}{3^{1006}} \right\rfloor$. Show that the polynomial
$$
Q(x) = a x^{2n+2} + a + \sum_{i=1}^{n} b_i x^{2(n-i+1)}
$$
has no rational root.

negatives.text:
Let $b_1, b_2, \dots, b_n$ be integers such that $\sum_{i=1}^{n} b_i = 2022$, and let $a$ be a divisor of $\left\lfloor \dfrac{2022!}{3^{1006}} \right\rfloor$. Prove that the polynomial
$$
U(x) = a x^{2n+2} + b_1 x^{2n} + b_2 x^{2n-2} + \dots + b_n x^2 - a
$$
has no rational root.

$$
V(x) = a x^{2n+1} + b_1 x^{2n} + b_2 x^{2n-2} + \dots + b_n x^2 + a
$$
has no rational root.

positive_text: Given that $a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$ are positive real numbers in non-increasing order and $b_1, b_2, \dots, b_n$ are positive real numbers such that for all $k = 1, 2, \dots, n$, the inequality $\prod_{i=1}^{k} b_i \ge \prod_{i=1}^{k} a_i$ holds, prove that $$\sum_{i=1}^{n} b_i \ge \sum_{i=1}^{n} a_i.$$

negatives.text: Let $a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$ and $b_1, b_2, \dots, b_n$ be positive real numbers with $a_1 \ge a_2 \ge \dots \ge a_n$ and $\sum_{i=1}^{k} b_i \ge \sum_{i=1}^{k} a_i$ for all $k = 1, 2, \dots, n$. Prove that $$\prod_{i=1}^{n} b_i \ge \prod_{i=1}^{n} a_i.$$

positive_text: Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle with $AB = AC$, and let $\ell$ be the internal angle bisector at $A$. Show that the line $TO$ contains the circumcenter of triangle $TPQ$.

negatives.text: Let $ABC$ be an isosceles acute triangle with $\ell$ the bisector of angle $A$. A circle with center $O$ passes through $B, C$ and intersects $AB, AC$ at $D, E$. positive_text: Let $ n $ be a positive integer. Consider a cube of side length $ 2n + 1 $, consisting of $ (2n + 1)^3 $ unit cubes. Each cube is colored either green or orange. It is given that in every subcube of size $ 2 \times 2 \times 2 $, at most 4 of the unit cubes are green. Determine the largest possible number of green cubes in the entire cube.

negatives.text: Let $ n $ be a positive integer. A cube of side length $ 2n + 1 $ is made of unit cubes, each colored green or orange. It is known that within any $ 2 \times 2 \times 2 $ subcube, there are at least 4 green cubes. What is the maximum number of green cubes in the entire cube?

positive_text: На лоптестој планети $X$ постоји $2n$ бензинских пумпи, где су сваке две пумпе спајане као дијаметрално супротни парови. На свакој пумпи је дата количина бензина. Знамо да аутомобил са празним (али довољно великим) резервоаром може увек стићи до дијаметрално упарене пумпе са било које пумпе, коришћењем бензина са других пумпи. Одредити све природне бројеве $n$ такве да увек постоји пумпа од које аутомобил може кренути са празним резервоаром и обићи све остале пумпе. (Аутомобил троши фиксну количину бензина по јединици пута.)

negatives.text: На планети $X$ облика лопте постоји $2n$ бензинских пумпи, где су сваке две пумпе упарене и на дијаметрално супротним тачкама. На свакој пумпи је дата количина бензина. Знамо да аутомобил са празним резервоаром може стићи до упарене пумпе са било које пумпе, али не и да обиђе све пумпе. Одредити све природне бројеве $n$ такве да увек постоји пумпа од које аутомобил може кренути и обићи све пумпе, ако му се дозволи да на неким пумпама узме дупло више бензина.

На планети $X$ постоји $2n$ бензинских пумпи, где су сваке две пумпе упарене и на дијаметрално супротним тачкама. На свакој пумпи је дата количина бензина. Знамо да аутомобил може стићи до упарене пумпе са било које пумпе. Одредити све природне бројеве $n$ такве да увек постоји пумпа од које аутомобил може кренути и обићи све пумпе, ако троши дупло више бензина на путу.

Знамо да аутомобил може стићи до упарене пумпе са било које пумпе, али не може да крене са пумпе и обиђе све пумпе ако бензин није увек доступан. positive_text: Let $x$, $y$, $z$, $w$ be positive integers such that $w$ divides $x^{2y} + z$ and $w \ge x + z$. Prove that $w \ge x + \sqrt[2y]{x}$.

negatives.text: Let $a$, $b$, $c$, $d$ be positive integers such that $d$ divides $a^{2b} + c$ and $d < a + c$. Prove that $d \ge a + \sqrt[2b]{a}$.
Let $a$, $b$, $c$, $d$ be positive integers such that $d$ divides $a^{2b} - c$ and $d \ge a + c$. Prove that $d \ge a + \sqrt[2b]{a}$.

positive_text: Let $ G $ be a finite directed graph with multiple directed edges allowed between any pair of vertices. Suppose that for any two directed paths from vertex $ A $ to vertex $ B $, there is at least one common edge used in both paths. Show that there exists a directed edge that is used in every path from $ A $ to $ B $.

negatives.text: In a finite network of cities with directed roads (multiple roads allowed in either direction), suppose that for any two paths from city $ A $ to city $ B $, they share at least one city (other than $ A $ or $ B $). Prove that there exists a city that is used in every path from $ A $ to $ B $.

In a finite network of cities with directed roads (multiple roads allowed in either direction), suppose that for any two paths from city $ A $ to city $ B $, they share at least one road in opposite directions. Prove that there exists a road that is used in every path from $ A $ to $ B $.

In a finite network of cities with directed roads (multiple roads allowed in either direction), suppose that for any two paths from city $ A $ to city $ B $, they differ by at least one road. Prove that there exists a road that is used in every path from $ A $ to $ B $.

positive_text:
Show that in any set of 42 numbers within the range $[1, 10^6]$, there exist four numbers such that for all permutations $(a, b, c, d)$ of these numbers, the inequality
$$
25(ab + cd)(ad + bc) \geq 16(ac + bd)^2
$$
always holds.

negatives.text:
Prove that among every 42 numbers from the interval $[1, 10^6]$ it is possible to choose four numbers in such a way that for any permutation $(a, b, c, d)$ of these numbers, the following inequality holds:
$$
25(ab + cd)(ad + bc) \leq 16(ac + bd)^2.
$$

Prove that among every 42 numbers from the interval $[1, 10^6]$ it is possible to choose four numbers in such a way that for any permutation $(a, b, c, d)$ of these numbers, the following inequality holds:
$$
25(ab + cd)(ad + bc) \geq 16(ac^2 + bd)^2.
$$

Prove that among every 42 numbers from the interval $[1, 10^6]$ it is possible to choose four numbers in such a way that for any permutation $(a, b, c, d)$ of these numbers, the following inequality holds:
$$
25(ab + cd)(ad + bc) \geq 16(ac + bd)^3.
$$

positive_text: Let $ABCD$ be a cyclic quadrilateral with circumcircle $\omega$. Let $K$ be the intersection of rays $AB$ and $DC$. Choose point $L$ on $BD$ such that $\angle BAC = \angle DAL$. Let $M$ be the point on $KL$ such that $CM$ is parallel to $BD$. Show that $BM$ is tangent to $\omega$.

negatives.text: Let $ABCD$ be a cyclic quadrilateral inscribed in circle $\omega$. Rays $AB$ and $DC$ meet at $K$. Let $L$ be on $BD$ such that $\angle BAC = \angle DAL$. Point $M$ lies on $KL$ such that $CM \parallel BD$. Prove that $BM$ is perpendicular to the tangent at $B$ of $\omega$.

positive_text: Let $ABCD$ be a cyclic quadrilateral with $BD$ as the diameter of the circumscribed circle. Let $A'$ be the reflection of $A$ over $BD$, and $B'$ be the reflection of $B$ over $AC$. If $P$ is the intersection of $A'C$ and $BD$, and $Q$ is the intersection of $B'D$ and $AC$, show that the line $PQ$ is perpendicular to $AC$.

negatives.text: Let $ABCD$ be a cyclic quadrilateral with $BD$ as the diameter of the circle. Let $A'$ be the reflection of $A$ over $BD$, and $B'$ be the reflection of $B$ over $AC$. If $P$ is the intersection of $A'C$ and $BD$, and $Q$ is the intersection of $B'D$ and $AC$, prove that $PQ$ is parallel to $AC$.

Let $ABCD$ be a cyclic quadrilateral with $BD$ as the diameter of the circle. Let $A'$ be the reflection of $A$ over $BD$, and $B'$ be the reflection of $B$ over $AC$. If $P$ is the intersection of $A'C$ and $BD$, and $Q$ is the intersection of $B'D$ and $AC$, prove that $PQ$ is perpendicular to $BD$.

positive_text: Find the largest odd positive integer $ N $ such that all odd integers $ k $ satisfying $ 1 < k < N $ and $ \gcd(k, N) = 1 $ are prime numbers.

negatives.text: Determine the largest odd positive integer $ N $ such that every odd integer $ k $ with $ 1 < k < N $ and $ (k, N) > 1 $ is a prime.
Determine the largest odd positive integer $ N $ such that every odd integer $ k $ with $ 1 < k < N $ and $ (k, N) = 1 $ is a composite number.
Determine the largest odd positive integer $ N $ such that every odd integer $ k $ with $ 1 < k < N $ and $ (k, N) = 1 $ is a prime power.

positive_text: Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle with circumcircle $\omega$. A point $M$ lies on side $BC$, and the line $AM$ intersects $\omega$ again at $Q$. The tangent at $Q$ to $\omega$ meets the line through $M$ perpendicular to the diameter $AK$ at a point $P$. If $L$ is the second point of tangency from $P$ to $\omega$, show that $L$, $M$, and $K$ are collinear.

negatives.text: In an acute-angled triangle $ABC$, $M$ is a point on side $BC$, and $AM$ intersects the circumcircle $\omega$ of $ABC$ again at $Q$. The tangent to $\omega$ at $Q$ intersects the line through $M$ parallel to the diameter $AK$ of $\omega$ at the point $P$. Let $L$ be the point on $\omega$ distinct from $Q$ such that $PL$ is tangent to $\omega$ at $L$. Prove that $L$, $M$ and $K$ are collinear.

In an acute triangle $ABC$ with circumcircle $\omega$, let $M$ be a point on side $BC$, and let $Q$ be the second intersection of $AM$ with $\omega$. The tangent to $\omega$ at $Q$ intersects the line through $M$ perpendicular to the diameter $AK$ at $P$. If $L$ is the second point of tangency from $P$ to $\omega$, prove that $K$, $L$, and the midpoint of $BC$ are collinear.

positive_text: Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle and let $AD$ be the angle bisector of $\angle BAC$, with $D$ on side $BC$. Drop perpendiculars from $D$ to $AB$ and $AC$, and let the feet of these perpendiculars be $E$ and $F$, respectively. Let $K$ be the intersection of $BF$ and $CE$. Show that $AK \perp BC$.

negatives.text: In an acute-angled triangle $ABC$, $D$ is the point on $BC$ such that $AD$ bisects $\angle BAC$, $E$ and $F$ are the feet of the perpendiculars from $D$ onto $AB$ and $AC$ respectively. The segments $BF$ and $CE$ intersect at $K$. Prove that $AK$ is parallel to $BC$.

In an acute-angled triangle $ABC$, $D$ is the point on $BC$ such that $AD$ bisects $\angle BAC$, $E$ and $F$ are the feet of the perpendiculars from $D$ onto $AB$ and $AC$ respectively. The segments $BF$ and $CE$ intersect at $K$. Prove that $AK$ is perpendicular to $AB$.

In an acute-angled triangle $ABC$, $D$ is the point on $BC$ such that $AD$ bisects $\angle BAC$, $E$ and $F$ are the feet of the perpendiculars from $D$ onto $AB$ and $AC$ respectively. The segments $BF$ and $CE$ intersect at $K$. Prove that $AK$ is equal in length to $BC$.

positive_text: On an island, every intersection has exactly three roads. A boy begins at his house and walks along the roads, turning left or right at each intersection in an alternating pattern (..., left, right, left, ...). Show that he will return to his house.

negatives.text: On an island, every junction has three roads. A boy begins at home and turns either left or right at each junction, but not in a fixed alternating pattern. Prove that he will eventually return to his home.
A boy lives on an island with four roads at each junction. He starts from home and alternates his turns (..., left, right, left, ...). Prove that he will eventually return to his home.
On an island, every junction has three roads. A boy starts at home and always turns left at each junction. Prove that he will eventually return to his home.

positive_text: Let $S$ be a subset of $\{1, 2, \ldots, 2015\}$ such that for any two distinct elements $a, b$ in $S$, the three values $a, b,$ and $c$ (where $c$ is either $a$ or $b$) form a unique isosceles triangle that is not equilateral. Determine the maximum possible number of elements in $S$.

negatives.text: Let $A$ be a set of numbers chosen from $1, 2, \ldots, 2015$ with the property that any two distinct numbers, say $x$ and $y$, in $A$ determine a unique equilateral triangle whose sides are of length $x$ or $y$. What is the largest possible size of $A$?

Let $A$ be a set of numbers chosen from $1, 2, \ldots, 2015$ with the property that any two distinct numbers, say $x$ and $y$, in $A$ determine a unique isosceles triangle (which is non-equilateral) whose sides are of length $x$ or $x + y$. What is the largest possible size of $A$?

Let $A$ be a set of numbers chosen from $1, 2, \ldots, 2015$ with the property that any two distinct numbers, say $x$ and $y$, in $A$ determine a unique isosceles triangle (which is non-equilateral) whose sides are of length $x$ or $2y$. What is the largest possible size of $A$?

positive_text: Given a positive integer $n$, find the smallest number of straight lines that can be arranged in the plane such that their intersections produce precisely $n$ unique points.

negatives.text: Let $n$ be a positive integer. Determine the minimum number of lines that can be drawn on the plane so that they intersect in at least $n$ distinct points.
Let $n$ be a positive integer. Determine the minimum number of lines that can be drawn on the plane so that they intersect in at most $n$ distinct points.
Let $n$ be a positive integer. Determine the minimum number of lines that can be drawn on the plane so that they intersect in at least $n^2$ distinct points.

positive_text: Let $p$ be a prime number. Prove that there exists a rearrangement $b_1, b_2, \dots, b_p$ of $1, 2, \dots, p$ such that the sequence $b_1, b_1b_2, \dots, b_1b_2 \dots b_p$ consists of distinct residues modulo $p$.

negatives.text: Let $n$ be a prime number. Show that there is a permutation $a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$ of $1, 2, \dots, n$ so that $a_1, a_1a_2, \dots, a_1a_2 \dots a_n$ are all divisible by $n$.

Let $n$ be a prime number. Show that there is a permutation $a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$ of $1, 2, \dots, n$ so that $a_1^2, a_1^2a_2^2, \dots, a_1^2a_2^2 \dots a_n^2$ leave distinct remainders when divided by $n$.

Let $n$ be a prime number. Show that there is a permutation $a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$ of $1, 2, \dots, n$ so that $a_1 + a_2, a_1 + a_2 + a_3, \dots, a_1 + a_2 + \dots + a_n$ leave distinct remainders when divided by $n$.

positive_text: Let $\omega$ be the incircle of $\triangle ABC$, tangent to sides $BC$, $CA$, and $AB$ at points $D$, $E$, and $F$, respectively. Let $\Gamma$ be a circle passing through $A$ and $B$ and enclosing $\triangle ABC$, intersecting the line $DE$ at $P$ and $Q$. Prove that the midpoint of segment $AB$ lies on the circumcircle of $\triangle PQF$.

negatives.text: The incircle of $\triangle ABC$ touches the sides $BC$, $CA$, $AB$, at $D$, $E$, $F$ respectively. A circle through $A$ and $B$ encloses $\triangle ABC$ and intersects the line $EF$ at points $P$ and $Q$. Prove that the midpoint of $AB$ lies on the circumcircle of $\triangle PQF$.

The incircle of $\triangle ABC$ touches the sides $BC$, $CA$, $AB$, at $D$, $E$, $F$ respectively. A circle through $A$ and $C$ encloses $\triangle ABC$ and intersects the line $DE$ at points $P$ and $Q$. Prove that the midpoint of $AB$ lies on the circumcircle of $\triangle PQF$.

The incircle of $\triangle ABC$ touches the sides $BC$, $CA$, $AB$, at $D$, $E$, $F$ respectively. A circle through $A$ and $B$ encloses $\triangle ABC$ and intersects the segment $DE$ at points $P$ and $Q$. Prove that the midpoint of $AC$ lies on the circumcircle of $\triangle PQF$.

positive_text: Using an unlimited supply of equilateral triangles and squares, both with side length $1$, construct a convex polygon with $n$ sides. If at least one triangle and one square must be used, what are the possible values of $n$?

negatives.text: You are given some equilateral triangles and squares, all with side length $1$, and asked to form a convex $n$-sided polygon using these pieces. If at least one triangle and one square must be used, and all vertices must have equal angles, what are the possible values of $n$?

positive_text: Let $\vec{a} = (a_1, a_2, ..., a_n)$ be an integer $n$-tuple. Suppose that for any guess $\vec{x} = (x_1, x_2, ..., x_n)$, the value $\prod_{i=1}^n (a_i - x_i)$ is revealed. What is the minimum number of guesses required for someone to determine $\vec{a}$ unambiguously?

negatives.text: Anana has an ordered $n$-tuple $(a_1, a_2, ..., a_n)$ of integers. Banana may make a guess on Anana's ordered integer $n$-tuple $(x_1, x_2, ..., x_n)$, upon which Anana will reveal the sum of differences $(a_1 - x_1) + (a_2 - x_2) + \cdots + (a_n - x_n)$. How many guesses does Banana need to figure out Anana's $n$-tuple for certain?

Anana has an ordered $n$-tuple $(a_1, a_2, ..., a_n)$ of integers. Banana may make a guess on Anana's ordered integer $n$-tuple $(x_1, x_2, ..., x_n)$, upon which Anana will reveal the product of absolute differences $|a_1 - x_1||a_2 - x_2|\cdots|a_n - x_n|$. How many guesses does Banana need to figure out Anana's $n$-tuple for certain?

Anana has an ordered $n$-tuple $(a_1, a_2, ..., a_n)$ of integers. Banana may make a guess on Anana's ordered integer $n$-tuple $(x_1, x_2, ..., x_n)$, upon which Anana will reveal the product of squared differences $(a_1 - x_1)^2(a_2 - x_2)^2\cdots(a_n - x_n)^2$. How many guesses does Banana need to figure out Anana's $n$-tuple for certain?

positive_text: Let a domino be a $1 \times 2$ tile. A $2023 \times 2023$ board is tiled with dominoes, with one square left empty. John moves dominoes into the empty space one at a time, ensuring each domino is moved at most once. What is the greatest number of dominoes that John could move in total?

negatives.text: A $2023 \times 2023$ grid is filled with $1 \times 2$ dominoes, leaving one square as an empty space. John moves dominoes into the empty square in a sequence, but now each domino can be moved multiple times. What is the maximum number of times a domino could have been moved?

A $2023 \times 2023$ grid is fully covered with $1 \times 2$ dominoes, with one square left as a gap. John slides dominoes out of the gap, rather than into it. Each domino is moved at most once. What is the maximum number of domino moves John could perform?

A $2024 \times 2024$ grid is filled with $1 \times 2$ dominoes, leaving one square as a gap. John slides dominoes into the gap, with each domino moved at most once. What is the maximum number of domino moves he could perform?

positive_text: Let triangle $ABC$ be a right triangle with legs of equal length and area $1$. Determine the minimal length of a line segment that partitions the triangle into two regions of equal area.

negatives.text: Let $ABC$ be an isosceles right-angled triangle of area $1$. Find the length of the shortest segment that divides the triangle into two regions of equal perimeter.
Let $ABC$ be an isosceles right-angled triangle of area $1$. Find the length of the shortest segment that divides the triangle into two regions with the ratio of areas $1:3$.
Let $ABC$ be an isosceles right-angled triangle of area $1$. Find the length of the shortest segment that divides the triangle into two regions of equal area and equal perimeter.

positive_text: Let $S$ be a square of area $27$. If $7$ triangles, each of area $7$, are placed within $S$, show that at least two of them have an overlapping region with area $\geq 1$.

negatives.text: Seven triangles of area $7$ lie inside a square of area $27$. Prove that among the $7$ triangles there are $2$ that intersect in a region of area less than $1$.

Seven triangles of area $7$ lie inside a square of area $27$. Prove that among the $7$ triangles there are $2$ that intersect in a region of area greater than $1$.

positive_text: Determine the minimal $ m > 0 $ such that a regular $ m $-gon allows selection of 8 vertices with no subset of three forming an isosceles triangle.

negatives.text: Find the smallest positive $ m $ so that it is possible to choose 8 vertices from a regular polygon with $ m $ sides such that no three of them are the vertices of an equilateral triangle.
Find the smallest positive $ m $ so that it is possible to choose 8 vertices from a regular polygon with $ m $ sides such that no three of them are the vertices of a right triangle.
Find the smallest positive $ m $ so that it is possible to choose 8 vertices from a regular polygon with $ m $ sides such that no three of them form an isosceles triangle with a given base length.

positive_text: Let $ABCD$ be a convex quadrilateral with diagonals intersecting at point $M$. A line through $M$ intersects side $AB$ at $P$ and side $CD$ at $Q$. Determine all such quadrilaterals for which the segment $PQ$ creates four similar triangles within $\triangle ABM$ and $\triangle CDM$.

negatives.text: Let $ABCD$ be a convex quadrilateral with diagonals intersecting at $M$. A line through $M$ intersects side $AB$ at $P$ and side $CD$ at $Q$. Find all the quadrilaterals so that the segment $PQ$ divides the triangles $ABM$ and $CDM$ into 4 congruent triangles.

Let $ABCD$ be a convex quadrilateral with diagonals intersecting at $M$. A line through $M$ intersects side $AB$ at $P$ and side $AD$ at $Q$. Find all the quadrilaterals so that the segment $PQ$ divides the triangles $ABM$ and $CDM$ into 4 similar triangles.

Let $ABCD$ be a convex quadrilateral with diagonals intersecting at $M$. A line through $M$ intersects side $AB$ at $P$ and side $CD$ at $Q$. Find all the quadrilaterals so that the segment $PQ$ divides the triangles $ABM$ and $CDM$ into 4 triangles with equal areas.

positive_text: Na $8 \times 8$ tabli želimo pobarvati minimalno število polj, tako da v vsaki konfiguraciji, ki ustreza obliki črke L, bo vsaj eno pobarvano polje. Določi to število.

negatives.text: Določi najmanjše število pobarvanih polj na tabli $8 \times 8$, tako da vsaka L-oblika vsebuje vsaj dva pobarvana polja.
Določi najmanjše število pobarvanih polj na tabli $8 \times 8$, tako da vsaka L-oblika vsebuje vsaj eno pobarvano polje, vendar L-oba lika imata nasprotno orientacijo.

positive_text: Oče želi poravnati 14560 SIT med tremi sinovi, pri čemer je vsak izmed njih prejel $\frac{6}{5}$ zneska, ki ga je prejel njegov mlajši brat. Določi zneske, ki jih je prejel vsak sin.

negatives.text: Oče želi razdeliti 14560 SIT med tremi sinovi, pri čemer vsak naslednji prejme $20 \%$ manj od prejšnjega. Določi zneske, ki jih je prejel vsak sin.

positive_text: Določi najmanjše število zvezdic, ki jih moramo postaviti v matriko $4 \times 4$, da bo po izbrisu poljubnih 2 stolpcev in 2 vrstic ostala vsaj ena zvezdica v preostali matriki.

negatives.text: Najmanj koliko zvezdic moramo narisati v tabelo velikosti $4 \times 4$, da bo po brisanju poljubnih 2 stolpcev in 2 vrstic ostalo v tabeli največ 1 zvezdica?

positive_text: Sea $A$ una matriz cuadrada de tamaño $3 \times 3$ con entradas en $\mathbb{R}$. Diremos que $A$ tiene suma uniforme si todas sus filas, columnas y diagonales suman lo mismo. positive_text: Dado un número real $a$, se define la sucesión $a, a_{2}, a_{3}, \ldots$ mediante la fórmula $$a_{n+1} = a_{n} \left(a_{n} + \frac{1}{n} \right) \text{ para } n \geq 1$$ Mostrar que hay un único valor de $a$ tal que $0 < a_{n} < a_{n+1} < 1$ para todo $n$.

positive_text: Sea $ C $ una cruz griega compuesta de cinco cuadrados iguales dispuestos en forma de cruz. Dividir $ C $ en cuatro regiones tal que estas puedan reordenarse para formar un cuadrado. positive_text:

positive_text: Dado un conjunto de $n$ puntos en el plano, tal que no hay dos pares de puntos con la misma distancia. Para cada punto, se conecta mediante un segmento con su vecino más cercano. Probar que ningún punto puede estar conectado a más de cinco otros puntos.

\frac{\text{\# estados buenos}}{\text{\# total de estados}} = \frac{3 \cdot 5 \cdot 7 \cdots (2n-1)}{2^n n!}

$$
\frac{\text{\# estados buenos}}{\text{\# total de estados}} = \frac{3 \cdot 5 \cdot 7 \cdots (2n-1)}{2^n n!}
$$

(i) 國王順時針逐一握手丈夫, 每次握手時, 皇后會跳到對應的妻子處握手。當國王回到起點時, 皇后已完成 $a$ 圈。
(ii) 皇后順時針逐一握手妻子, 每次握手時, 國王會跳到對應的丈夫處握手。當皇后回到起點時, 國王已完成 $b$ 圈。
求 $|a - b|$ 的最大值。

positive_text: 令 $\mathbb{P}$ 表所有正整數之集合，$\mathbb{Z}$ 表所有整數之集合。試求所有函數 $f: \mathbb{P} \to \mathbb{Z}$ 滿足: 對所有 $n, m \in \mathbb{P}$，$n \mid f(m)$ 若且唯若 $m \mid \sum_{d|n} f(d)$。

negatives.text: 令 $f: \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{Z}$ 為一函數。若對所有 $n, m \in \mathbb{N}$，$n$ 整除 $f(m)$ 若且唯若 $m$ 整除 $\sum_{d|n} f(d) + 1$，求所有可能的 $f$。

positive_text:
設 $n$ 是自然數, $A$ 和 $B$ 是互質的正整數, 且
$$
\prod_{k=1}^{n} \frac{k!}{(2k)!} \cdot \left(\frac{n(n+1)}{2}\right)! = \frac{B}{A}.
$$
試證 $A$ 是 $2$ 的某次方。

negatives.text:
設 $n$ 是正整數, $A$ 和 $B$ 是互質的正整數, 且
$$
\left(\frac{n(n+1)}{2}\right)! \cdot \prod_{k=1}^{n} \frac{(2k)!}{k!} = \frac{B}{A}.
$$
試證 $A$ 是 $2$ 的某次方。

設 $n$ 是正整數, $A$ 和 $B$ 是互質的正整數, 且
$$
\left(\frac{n(n+1)}{2}\right)! \cdot \prod_{k=1}^{n} \frac{k!}{(2k+1)!} = \frac{B}{A}.
$$
試證 $A$ 是 $2$ 的某次方。

設 $n$ 是正整數, $A$ 和 $B$ 是互質的正整數, 且
$$
\left(\frac{n(n+1)}{2}\right)! + \prod_{k=1}^{n} \frac{k!}{(2k)!} = \frac{B}{A}.
$$
試證 $A$ 是 $2$ 的某次方。

positive_text:
令 $p$ 和 $q$ 為相異正整數。考慮一個無限大的棋盤, 其中每一格可填入非負整數。初始時所有格子皆為空。我們進行如下操作:
(1) 若棋盤上存在重複的數字, 則選出一對相同數字, 將其中之一加上 $p$, 另一個加上 $q$。
(2) 若棋盤上沒有重複數字, 則在兩個尚未使用的格子中填入 $0$。
證明: 無論操作過程如何, 必然存在某一時刻後, 只能執行操作 (1)。

positive_text:
Let $\mathbb{N}$ be the set of positive integers. Define
$$
A = \{2^a + a^2 \mid a \in \mathbb{N}\}
$$
and define a sequence of functions $\{h_i\}_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$ from $\mathbb{N}$ to $\mathbb{R}^+$ by
$$
h_1(n) = n + \log_2 n, \quad h_{i+1}(n) = n + \log_2 h_i(n), \quad \forall i \in \mathbb{N}.
$$
Prove that there exists an injective function $g : \mathbb{R}^+ \to \mathbb{R}^+$ such that:
(a) For all $i, n \in \mathbb{N}$, the expression $n + \lfloor g(h_i(n)) \rfloor$ is never in $A$.
(b) For every $k \in \mathbb{N} \setminus A$ and $i \in \mathbb{N}$, there exists a unique $a_{k,i} \in \mathbb{N}$ such that
$$
a_{k,i} + \lfloor g(h_i(a_{k,i})) \rfloor = k, \quad \forall i \in \mathbb{N}.
$$
$\lfloor x \rfloor$ denotes the floor function of $x$.

positive_text: Let $ABCD$ be a convex quadrilateral such that $\angle ABC$ and $\angle CDA$ are both obtuse, and $\angle DAB = \angle BCD$. Let $E$ and $F$ be the reflections of $A$ across $BC$ and $CD$, respectively. If lines $AE$ and $AF$ intersect $BD$ at $K$ and $L$, show that the circumcircles of $\triangle BEK$ and $\triangle DFL$ are tangent.

Prove that the circumcircles of triangles $BEK$ and $DFL$ are tangent to each other.

positive_text: Let $\{A_i = (x_i, y_i) : i = 1, \dots, 2020\}$ be points in the plane with $x_1 = 0 < x_2 < \dots < x_{2020}$ and $y_{2020} = 0 < y_{2019} < \dots < y_1$. Define $O = (0, 0)$, and consider the polygon $C$ formed by connecting $O$ to $A_1$, $A_1$ to $A_2$, ..., $A_{2020}$ back to $O$. Tao wishes to blacken the region $C$ by selecting points $(x, y)$ and paying $xy$ dollars to blacken the rectangle $\{(x', y') : 0 \le x' \le x, 0 \le y' \le y\}$. Prove that Tao can cover the whole $C$ with cost at most $4|C|$, where $|C|$ is the area of the polygon.

negatives.text: Let $\{A_i = (x_i, y_i) : i = 1, \dots, 2020\}$ satisfy $x_1 = 0 < x_2 < \dots < x_{2020}$ and $y_1 = 0 < y_2 < \dots < y_{2020}$. Define polygon $C$ as the closed region formed by connecting $O = (0, 0)$ to $A_1$, $A_1$ to $A_2$, ..., $A_{2020}$ to $O$. Tao can choose a point $(x, y)$, pay $xy$ dollars, and paint the rectangle $\{(x', y') : 0 \le x' \le x, 0 \le y' \le y\}$. Prove that Tao can paint the entire region $C$ for a cost of at most $4|C|$, where $|C|$ is the area of $C$.

Define polygon $C$ as the closed figure formed by connecting $O = (0, 0)$ to $A_1$, $A_1$ to $A_2$, ..., $A_{2020}$ to $O$. Tao can choose a point $(x, y)$, pay $xy$ dollars, and paint the rectangle $\{(x', y') : 0 \le x' \le x, 0 \le y' \le y\}$. Let $\{A_i = (x_i, y_i) : i = 1, \dots, 2020\}$ satisfy $x_1 = 0 < x_2 < \dots < x_{2020}$ and $y_{2020} < y_{2019} < \dots < y_1$, with $y_{2020} = 0$. positive_text:
Let $n$ be a fixed positive integer. A positive integer $m$ is defined to be $n$-good if the number of distinct prime divisors $p$ with $p^2 \mid m$ is no more than $2n$.
(a) Suppose $\gcd(a, b) = 1$ for positive integers $a, b$. Prove there exist positive integers $x, y$ such that $ax^n + by^n$ is $n$-good.
(b) For any $k$ positive integers $a_1, \dots, a_k$ with $\gcd(a_1, \dots, a_k) = 1$, show there exist positive integers $x_1, \dots, x_k$ such that $\sum_{i=1}^k a_ix_i^n$ is $n$-good.

negatives.text:
Let $n$ be a given positive integer. A positive integer $m$ is $n$-good if it has at most $2n$ distinct prime divisors $p$ such that $p^2 \mid m$.
(a) Show that for any positive integers $a, b$ with $\gcd(a, b) = 1$, there exist positive integers $x, y$ such that $ax^n + by^n$ is $n$-bad.
(b) For any $k$ positive integers $a_1, \dots, a_k$ with $\gcd(a_1, \dots, a_k) = 1$, show there exist positive integers $x_1, \dots, x_k$ such that $\sum_{i=1}^k a_ix_i^n$ is $n$-bad.

Let $n$ be a given positive integer. A positive integer $m$ is $n$-good if it has at most $2n$ distinct prime divisors $p$ such that $p^2 \mid m$.
(a) Show that for any positive integers $a, b$ with $\gcd(a, b) = 1$, there exist positive integers $x, y$ such that $ax^n - by^n$ is $n$-good.
(b) For any $k$ positive integers $a_1, \dots, a_k$ with $\gcd(a_1, \dots, a_k) = 1$, show there exist positive integers $x_1, \dots, x_k$ such that $\sum_{i=1}^k a_ix_i^n$ is $n$-good.

Let $n$ be a given positive integer. A positive integer $m$ is $n$-good if it has at most $2n$ distinct prime divisors $p$ such that $p^2 \mid m$.
(a) Show that for any positive integers $a, b$ with $\gcd(a, b) = 1$, there exist positive integers $x, y$ such that $a x^n + b y^n$ is $n$-good and divisible by $n$.
(b) For any $k$ positive integers $a_1, \dots, a_k$ with $\gcd(a_1, \dots, a_k) = 1$, show there exist positive integers $x_1, \dots, x_k$ such that $\sum_{i=1}^k a_ix_i^n$ is $n$-good and divisible by $n$.

positive_text:

動物每次同時移動一步，根據其方向前進；若超出範圍，則透過模 $2n$ 計算座標，使得 $p \equiv i \pmod{2n}$ 且 $q \equiv j \pmod{2n}$。

傑夫希望所有保留的動物在每回合中，不會有兩隻動物抵達同一點，也不會互為對方的目標點。

試證：不論動物的初始方向如何，傑夫總能實現此目標。

positive_text: Let $n$ be a positive integer. If there exist three distinct positive divisors $a, b, c$ of $n$ such that $a + b + c = 2022$, find the smallest such $n$.

negatives.text: A positive integer is said to be **so-last-year** if it has three distinct positive divisors whose product is equal to $2022$. Determine the smallest so-last-year number.

positive_text: Let $\Omega$ be the circumcircle of an isosceles trapezoid $ABCD$ with $AD \parallel BC$. Let $X$ be the mirror image of $D$ over $BC$. Let $Q$ be a point on the arc $BC$ of $\Omega$ that does not include $A$, and let $P = DQ \cap BC$. Suppose point $E$ satisfies $EQ \parallel PX$ and $\angle BEC$ is bisected by $EQ$. Show that $\angle AEP$ is also bisected by $EQ$.

negatives.text: Let $\Omega$ be the circumcircle of an isosceles trapezoid $ABCD$, with $AD \parallel BC$. Let $X$ be the reflection of $D$ over $BC$. Let $Q$ lie on the arc $BC$ of $\Omega$ that contains $A$. Let $P = DQ \cap BC$. Suppose $E$ is a point such that $EQ \parallel PX$ and $EQ$ bisects $\angle BEC$. positive_text: Let $x$ be a natural number in base 10. The product of the digits of $x$ is equal to $x^2 - 15x - 27$. Determine all such values of $x$.

negatives.text: A natural number $x$, when expressed in decimal notation, has the product of its digits equal to $x^2 + 15x - 27$. Find all possible $x$.

positive_text: Let $ABCD$ be a quadrilateral with diagonals $AC$ and $BD$ meeting at $E$, and let $F$ and $G$ be the intersections of $AB$ with $CD$ and $AD$ with $BC$ respectively. negatives.text: Let $ABCD$ be a quadrilateral with diagonals $AC$ and $BD$ intersecting at $E$, and let $F$ and $G$ be the intersections of $AB$ with $CD$ and $AD$ with $BC$, respectively. Let $W, X, Y, Z$ be the reflections of $E$ over $AB, BC, CD, DA$. Prove that the intersection of $\odot(FWY)$ and $\odot(GXZ)$ lies on the line $FE$.

positive_text: Let triangle $ABC$ have the angle bisector of $\angle BAC$, the median from $B$, and the perpendicular bisector of segment $AB$ meeting at point $X$. If $H$ is the orthocenter of triangle $ABC$, prove that $\angle BXH = 90^\circ$.

negatives.text: Let $ABC$ be a triangle such that the internal angle trisector of $\angle BAC$, the $B$-median and the perpendicular bisector of $AB$ intersect at a single point $X$. Let $H$ be the orthocenter of $ABC$. Show that $\angle BXH = 90^\circ$.

Let $ABC$ be a triangle such that the internal angle bisector of $\angle BAC$, the $B$-median and the perpendicular bisector of $AC$ intersect at a single point $X$. Let $H$ be the orthocenter of $ABC$. Show that $\angle BXH = 90^\circ$.

Let $ABC$ be a triangle such that the internal angle bisector of $\angle BAC$, the $B$-median and the perpendicular bisector of $AB$ intersect at a single point $X$. Let $H$ be the orthocenter of $ABC$. Show that $\angle ABH = 90^\circ$.

positive_text: Let $P$ be a point inside triangle $\triangle ABC$. Define points $A_1, B_1, C_1$ on the segments $PA, PB, PC$ respectively, such that they lie strictly between $P$ and the corresponding vertices. Let $A_2 = \overline{BC_1} \cap \overline{CB_1}$, $B_2 = \overline{CA_1} \cap \overline{AC_1}$, and $C_2 = \overline{AB_1} \cap \overline{BA_1}$. Let $U = A_1B_1 \cap A_2B_2$, and $V = A_1C_1 \cap A_2C_2$. Prove that the lines $UC_2$, $VB_2$, and $AP$ meet at a single point.

negatives.text: Let $P$ be a point inside $\triangle ABC$. Let $A_1, B_1, C_1$ be points in the interiors of the segments $PA, PB, PC$, respectively. Let $\overline{BC_1} \cap \overline{CB_1} = \{A_2\}$, $\overline{CA_1} \cap \overline{AC_1} = \{B_2\}$, and $\overline{AB_1} \cap \overline{BA_1} = \{C_2\}$. Let $U$ be the intersection of the lines $A_1B_1$ and $A_2B_2$, and $V$ be the intersection of the lines $A_1C_1$ and $A_2C_2$. Show that the lines $UC_2$, $VB_2$, and $PC$ are concurrent.

Let $P$ be a point inside $\triangle ABC$. Let $A_1, B_1, C_1$ be points in the interiors of the segments $PA, PB, PC$, respectively. Let $\overline{BC_1} \cap \overline{CB_1} = \{A_2\}$, $\overline{CA_1} \cap \overline{AC_1} = \{B_2\}$, and $\overline{AB_1} \cap \overline{BA_1} = \{C_2\}$. Let $U$ be the intersection of the lines $A_1B_1$ and $A_2B_2$, and $V$ be the intersection of the lines $A_1C_1$ and $A_2C_2$. Show that the lines $UC_2$, $VB_2$, and $AP$ are parallel.

Let $P$ be a point inside $\triangle ABC$. Let $A_1, B_1, C_1$ be points in the interiors of the segments $PA, PB, PC$, respectively. Let $\overline{BC_1} \cap \overline{CB_1} = \{A_2\}$, $\overline{CA_1} \cap \overline{AC_1} = \{B_2\}$, and $\overline{AB_1} \cap \overline{BA_1} = \{C_2\}$. Let $U$ be the intersection of the lines $A_1B_1$ and $A_2B_2$, and $V$ be the intersection of the lines $A_1C_1$ and $A_2C_2$. Show that the lines $UC_2$, $VB_2$, and $AP$ are perpendicular.

positive_text: Let $S$ be a subset of a square with side length $5$ such that no two points in $S$ are at distances $0.001$, $\sqrt{3} \cdot 0.002$, or $0.002$ apart. Show that the area of $S$ is at most $3.575$.

negatives.text: In a square of side length $5$, a figure is placed such that the distance between any two of its points is not equal to $0.001$, $0.002 \times \sqrt{3}$, $0.002$. Prove that the area of this figure does not exceed $3.576$.

positive_text: Suppose all points in the plane are assigned one of two colors: red or blue. Prove that there is a monochromatic triangle with sides of length $\sqrt{3}$, $1$, and $2$.

negatives.text: Each point of the plane is colored either red or blue. Show that there exists a triangle with side lengths $1$, $2$, and $\sqrt{5}$, and its three vertices are of the same color.
Each point of the plane is colored either red or blue. Show that there exists a triangle with side lengths $1$, $2$, and $\sqrt{3}$, and its three vertices are of different colors.
Each point of the plane is colored either red or blue. Show that there exists a triangle with side lengths $1$, $2$, and $\sqrt{3}$, and at least two of its vertices are of the same color.

positive_text:
Let $P(x) = c_{2016}x^{2016} + c_{2015}x^{2015} + \dots + c_1x + c_0$ be a degree $2016$ polynomial, where the sum of its odd-indexed coefficients satisfies
$$
|c_1 + c_3 + \dots + c_{2015}| > |c_0 + c_2 + \dots + c_{2016}|.
$$
Show that the number of roots of $P(x)$ with $|x| < 1$ is odd (counting multiplicity).

negatives.text:
Let $P(x) = a_{2016}x^{2016} + a_{2015}x^{2015} + \dots + a_1x + a_0$ be a degree $2016$ polynomial, where the coefficients satisfy
$$
|a_1 + a_3 + \dots + a_{2015}| < |a_0 + a_2 + \dots + a_{2016}|.
$$
Prove that the number of roots of $P(x)$ with absolute value less than $1$ is odd (roots are counted with multiplicity).

Let $P(x) = a_{2016}x^{2016} + a_{2015}x^{2015} + \dots + a_1x + a_0$ be a degree $2016$ polynomial, where the coefficients satisfy
$$
|a_1 + a_3 + \dots + a_{2015}| > |a_0 + a_2 + \dots + a_{2016}|.
$$
Prove that the number of roots of $P(x)$ with absolute value less than or equal to $1$ is odd (roots are counted with multiplicity).

Let $P(x) = a_{2016}x^{2016} + a_{2015}x^{2015} + \dots + a_1x + a_0$ be a degree $2016$ polynomial, where the coefficients satisfy
$$
|a_1 + a_3 + \dots + a_{2015}| > |a_0 + a_2 + \dots + a_{2016}|.
$$
Prove that the number of real roots of $P(x)$ with absolute value less than $1$ is odd (roots are counted with multiplicity).

positive_text: Let $ABCD$ be a cyclic quadrilateral with circumcenter $O$. Let $G$ be the intersection of the diagonals $AC$ and $BD$. Let $P, Q, R, S$ be the centers of the circles passing through $AGB, BGC, CGD, DGA$, respectively. If $PR$ and $QS$ intersect at $M$, prove that $M$ lies at the midpoint of $G$ and $O$.

negatives.text: Let $ABCD$ be a cyclic quadrilateral with circumcenter $O$. Let $G$ be the intersection of the diagonals $AC$ and $BD$. Let $P, Q, R, S$ be the circumcenters of triangles $AGB, BGC, CGD, DGA$ respectively. The lines $PQ$ and $RS$ intersect at $M$. Show that $M$ is the midpoint of $G$ and $O$.

Let $ABCD$ be a cyclic quadrilateral with circumcenter $O$. The diagonals $AC$ and $BD$ intersect at $G$. Let $P, Q, R, S$ be the circumcenters of triangles $AGB, BGC, CGD, DGA$ respectively. The lines $PR$ and $QS$ intersect at $M$. Show that $M$ is the midpoint of $G$ and the centroid of triangle $ABC$.

positive_text: Show whether it is possible to find $2017$ consecutive positive integers such that none of them can be expressed as the sum of two integer squares.

negatives.text: Prove or disprove that there exist $2017$ consecutive positive integers such that each can be written as $a^2 + b^2$ where $a$ and $b$ are integers.
Prove or disprove that there exist $2017$ consecutive positive integers such that each cannot be written as $a^2 + b^2$ where $a$ and $b$ are positive integers.
Prove or disprove that there exist $2017$ consecutive positive integers such that each cannot be written as $a^2 + b^2 + c^2$ where $a, b, c$ are integers.

positive_text: Let there be $2001$ individuals, each selecting an integer and referencing a subset of the others. For each individual, define two sums: $S_1$, the sum of integers chosen by those referenced by the individual, and $S_2$, the sum of integers chosen by those referencing the individual. The difference $S_1 - S_2$ is assigned to the individual. Can all such differences be positive?

negatives.text: Each of the $2001$ boys chooses an integer and makes a list by writing the names of some of the boys other than himself. For each boy, one computes the sum of the numbers which the boys whose names are included in this boy's list chose, as well as the sum of the numbers which the boys who included the name of this boy in their lists chose. The former sum is added to the latter one, and the resulting number is assigned to the boy in question. Determine whether or not these new numbers assigned to the $2001$ boys can all be positive.

The latter product is subtracted from the former one, and the resulting number is assigned to the boy in question. Determine whether or not these new numbers assigned to the $2001$ boys can all be positive.

positive_text: Let $AB$ be a diameter of a circle, and let $Q$ be a point on the circle, not coinciding with $A$ or $B$. Drop a perpendicular from $Q$ to $AB$, and let $H$ be the foot of this perpendicular. If a circle centered at $Q$ with radius $QH$ intersects the circle with diameter $AB$ at two points $C$ and $D$, show that the line $CD$ passes through the midpoint of $QH$.

negatives.text: Let $AB$ be a diameter of a circle and let $Q$ be a point on the circle distinct from $A$ and $B$. Let $H$ be the foot of the perpendicular from $Q$ to $AB$. Consider a circle centered at $Q$ with radius $QH$. If this circle intersects the original circle at points $C$ and $D$, prove that $CD$ is perpendicular to $QH$.

Let $AB$ be a diameter of a circle and let $Q$ be a point on the circle not equal to $A$ or $B$. Let $H$ be the foot of the perpendicular from $Q$ to $AB$. Consider a circle centered at $H$ with radius $QH$. If this circle intersects the original circle at points $C$ and $D$, prove that $CD$ bisects $QH$.

positive_text: Let triangle $ABC$ be acute, and let triangle $A_1B_1C_1$ be similar to it, with $B_1$ on ray $AC$, $C_1$ on ray $BA$, and $A_1$ on ray $CB$. Show that the orthocenter of triangle $A_1B_1C_1$ coincides with the circumcenter of triangle $ABC$.

negatives.text: Let triangle $ABC$ be acute, and suppose triangle $A_1B_1C_1$ is similar to triangle $A_2B_2C_2$, with $B_1$ on ray $AC$, $C_1$ on ray $BA$, and $A_1$ on ray $CB$. Prove that the orthocenter of triangle $A_1B_1C_1$ coincides with the circumcenter of triangle $ABC$.

positive_text: Let $\Gamma$ be a circle and $\ell$ a line in the plane that does not intersect $\Gamma$. Consider all points $A$ and $B$ on $\ell$ such that there exist points $P, Q, R, S$ on $\Gamma$ with $PQ \cap RS = \{A\}$ and $PS \cap QR = \{B\}$. negatives.text: Let $\Gamma$ be a circle and $\ell$ a line in the plane that does not intersect $\Gamma$. positive_text: Consider a graph with $2009$ vertices where every pair of vertices has exactly one common neighbor. Find the minimal possible value of the difference between the degrees of the vertex with the highest degree and the vertex with the lowest degree.

negatives.text: In a group of $2009$ people, any pair of persons have at least one common friend. Determine the smallest possible value of the difference between the numbers of friends of the person with the most friends and the person with the least friends.

positive_text: An undirected graph is connected, and after adding a single edge, the diameter of the graph becomes at most 17. What is the maximum possible diameter of the graph before the edge was added?

negatives.text: Graph Air (GA) is running two way flights between some cities of a country so that it is possible to travel between any two cities using GA flights. It turned out that after removing one flight, one may travel between any two cities by using at most 17 GA flights. Determine the maximal possible number (if exists) of GA flights necessary to use for traveling between any two cities of a country before removing the flight.

Graph Air (GA) is running two way flights between some cities of a country so that it is possible to travel between any two cities using GA flights. Determine the maximal possible number (if exists) of GA flights necessary to use for traveling between any two cities of a country before adding the flight, assuming the graph is a tree.

positive_text: Let $G$ be a $2013 \times 2013$ grid. A set of unit squares is marked such that every $19 \times 19$ subgrid of $G$ contains at least 21 marked squares. What is the minimum number of marked squares required?

negatives.text: Some unit squares of the grid $2013 \times 2013$ are marked so that any sub-square $19 \times 19$ of the grid has at most 21 marked unit squares. What is the maximum possible number of marked unit squares?

positive_text: Let $ABCD$ be a convex quadrilateral with diagonals intersecting at $E$. Suppose that $\angle EDC = \angle DEC = \angle BAD$. If a point $F$ lies on segment $BC$ such that $\angle BAF + \angle EBF = \angle BFE$, prove that the points $A, B, F, D$ lie on a circle.

negatives.text: Let $ABCD$ be a convex quadrilateral with diagonals intersecting at $E$. Suppose $\angle EDC = \angle DEC = \angle BAD$. If a point $F$ lies on segment $BC$ such that $\angle BAF - \angle EBF = \angle BFE$, prove that $A, B, F, D$ are concyclic.

positive_text: In triangle $ABC$, let the external angle bisector of $\angle A$ meet the ray $BC$ at $D$. Drop perpendiculars from $B$ and $C$ to the line $AD$, and let their feet be $E$ and $F$ respectively. Also, drop a perpendicular from $D$ to side $AC$, with foot at $G$. negatives.text: In triangle $ABC$, the internal bisector of $\angle BAC$ intersects the ray $[BC$ at $D$. Show that $\angle DGE + \angle DGF = 180^\circ$.

In triangle $ABC$, the external bisector of $\angle BAC$ intersects the ray $[BC$ at $D$. The feet of the perpendiculars from $B$ and $C$ to the line $AD$ are $E$ and $F$ respectively, and the foot of the perpendicular from $D$ to $AB$ is $G$. Show that $\angle DGE + \angle DGF = 180^\circ$.

In triangle $ABC$, the external bisector of $\angle BAC$ intersects the ray $[BC$ at $D$. The feet of the perpendiculars from $B$ and $C$ to the line $AD$ are $E$ and $F$ respectively, and the foot of the perpendicular from $D$ to $AC$ is $G$. Show that $\angle DGE + \angle DGF = 90^\circ$.

positive_text: Let triangle $ABC$ have circumcircle $\omega$, and for each vertex $A$, construct a circle $\omega_A$ outside $ABC$, tangent to $BC$ at $A_1$ and tangent to $\omega$ at $A_2$. Define $\omega_B$, $\omega_C$ and points $B_1, B_2, C_1, C_2$ similarly. negatives.text: Let triangle $ABC$ have circumcircle $\omega$. Let $\omega_A$ be a circle outside $ABC$ tangent to $BC$ at $A_1$ and tangent to $\omega$ at $A_2$. Let $\omega_B$, $\omega_C$ and points $B_1, B_2, C_1, C_2$ be defined similarly. Suppose the lines $AA_1$, $BB_1$, and $CC_1$ are parallel. positive_text: A *team* is defined as a group of 25 students where every pair is friends. It is known that each student is in at least one team, but if any pair of students cease to be friends, then at least one student becomes part of no team. A team is *special* if there exists at least one student in it with no friends outside the team. Prove that every pair of friends is part of some special team.

negatives.text: A *team* is a group of 25 students where all are friends. Suppose each student is in at least one team, but if any two students become enemies, then at least one student is left without a team. A team is *special* if at least one student in it has no friend outside the team. Prove that any two enemies belong to some special team.

Suppose each student is in at least one team, but if any two students cease being friends, then at least one student is left without any team. A team is *special* if all students in it have no friends outside the team. Prove that any two friends belong to some special team.

positive_text: In a $29 \times 29$ grid, rows and columns are labeled from $1$ to $29$ starting from the bottom and the left, respectively. Certain squares are marked. For any marked square, there is at most one other marked square such that its row and column indices are both greater than or equal to those of the first. Determine the maximum number of marked squares.

negatives.text: In a $29 \times 29$ grid, rows and columns are indexed from bottom to top and left to right, respectively. What is the maximum number of marked squares?

What is the maximum number of marked squares?

positive_text: Suppose there are $101$ students in a school, and each student has at least one friend among the others. Prove that for every integer $n$ such that $1 < n < 101$, there exists a subset of $n$ students where every student in the subset has at least one friend within the subset.

negatives.text: In a school with $101$ pupils, any pupil has at least one friend among the remaining pupils. Show that for each $1 < n < 101$, one can choose a group of $n$ pupils such that each pupil of the group has at least one friend outside the group.
